outlook.statement: India is poised for significant infrastructure growth driven by substantial government investments and increased private sector participation. The company will encash opportunities for growth and is currently executing projects in Chennai, Tuticorin, Jammu and Mumbai Airport with about Rs. 300 crores unfinished projects in hand.
Tarmat is in the process of securing new projects of about Rs.300 crores and there are on-going projects in Chennai, Mumbai and Jammu.

India's infrastructure sector is attracting rising investments, with government capital expenditure increasing 4.2 times to Rs. 12.20 lakh crore (US$121.29 billion) in FY 2026-27, strengthening roads, railways, ports and logistics growth nationwide.
Morgan Stanley projects India's infrastructure investment to rise from 5.03% of GDP in FY26 to 6.5% by financial year 2029.
